# Micah 4 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** It shall come to pass in the latter days that the mountain of the house of the LORD shall be established as the highest of the mountains, and it shall be lifted up above the hills; and peoples shall flow to it,

**2** And many nations shall come, and say: "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, that He may teach us His ways and that we may walk in His paths." For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

**3** He shall judge between many peoples, and shall decide disputes for strong nations far away; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks; nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war anymore;

**4** But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree, and no one shall make them afraid, for the mouth of the LORD of hosts has spoken.

**5** For all the peoples walk each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.

**6** "In that day," declares the LORD, "I will assemble the lame and gather those who have been driven away, and those I have afflicted. I will make the lame into a remnant and the far-removed into a strong nation, and the LORD will reign over them in Mount Zion from now and forevermore."

**7** "In that day," declares the LORD, "I will assemble the lame and gather those who have been driven away, and those I have afflicted. I will make the lame into a remnant and the far-removed into a strong nation, and the LORD will reign over them in Mount Zion from now and forevermore."

**8** "In that day," declares the LORD, "I will assemble the lame and gather those who have been driven away, and those I have afflicted. I will make the lame into a remnant and the far-removed into a strong nation, and the LORD will reign over them in Mount Zion from now and forevermore."

**9** "In that day," declares the LORD, "I will assemble the lame and gather those who have been driven away, and those I have afflicted. I will make the lame into a remnant and the far-removed into a strong nation, and the LORD will reign over them in Mount Zion from now and forevermore."

**10** "In that day," declares the LORD, "I will assemble the lame and gather those who have been driven away, and those I have afflicted. I will make the lame into a remnant and the far-removed into a strong nation, and the LORD will reign over them in Mount Zion from now and forevermore."

**11** "In that day," declares the LORD, "I will assemble the lame and gather those who have been driven away, and those I have afflicted. I will make the lame into a remnant and the far-removed into a strong nation, and the LORD will reign over them in Mount Zion from now and forevermore."

**12** "In that day," declares the LORD, "I will assemble the lame and gather those who have been driven away, and those I have afflicted. I will make the lame into a remnant and the far-removed into a strong nation, and the LORD will reign over them in Mount Zion from now and forevermore."

**13** "In that day," declares the LORD, "I will assemble the lame and gather those who have been driven away, and those I have afflicted. I will make the lame into a remnant and the far-removed into a strong nation, and the LORD will reign over them in Mount Zion from now and forevermore."

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- **4:1-5**: This oracle is the theological counterpart to 3:12. The Temple mount that will be 'plowed as a field' (3:12) will ultimately be 'established as the highest of mountains.' Destruction is penultimate; restoration is ultimate.

- **4:3**: The 'swords into plowshares' oracle is among the most quoted passages in the Bible. It envisions not merely ceasefire but the complete transformation of the instruments and knowledge of war.

- **4:4**: The vine-and-fig-tree image adds a dimension Isaiah's parallel lacks: individual security. The peace is not abstract but domestic — each person safe on their own land.

— LOGOS
